FACT The proof follows the Frobenius-style counting argument:
- If n = 0, the claim holds trivially.
- Otherwise there is an element of order p, so p divides |G|.
- Let Ω be the set of p-tuples in G with product 1. Then |Ω| = |G|^(p-1), which is divisible by p.
- Cyclic rotation acts on Ω with order p. The Mathlib congruence `Equiv.Perm.card_fixedPoints_modEq` gives |Ω| ≡ |Fix| (mod p).
- The fixed points are the constant tuples (g, …, g) with g^p = 1, so |Fix| = n + 1.
- Hence p divides n + 1.
